evidence: CONSTRUCTED — a hearing carrying 2 to 5 youth defendants is legal but not drawn from observed data

provenance.subscriptionsOrigin: cpp-context-azure-legalaidagency/azure-functions/durable-functions/NowsVariantsSubscriptions/test/subscriptions.json (five court-register entries, verbatim, including the one entry in the whole capture that covers court house B01LY00)
provenance.note: A child who survives every filter to the outbound document: youth-flagged, a youth date of birth, a middle name, both ethnicity descriptions, two defendantCaseJudicialResults so postHearingCustodyStatus reaches a real value, an associated defence organisation, a two-entry defendantAttendance with the youth's record SECOND (defect C8), and a prosecuting-authority court application.
provenance.operatorDescription: Clones the first defendant under fresh identifiers, so one hearing carries N register defendants.
provenance.operatorRationale: One register carries every youth defendant on the hearing (OutboundCourtRegister/index.js:22 filters, YouthDefendantMapper iterates), while the subscription match is decided ONCE from registerDefendants[0] (defect C31). Those two facts only interact at N >= 2, and a port that keys the match on the wrong defendant produces the right defendant COUNT with the wrong recipients — which is invisible at N = 1. Each clone gets fresh uuids for the defendant, its master defendant and its offences, so no identity is duplicated.
